thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: SRV resolution errors detected in us-west-3c. Multiple services reporting SRV lookup timeouts. Paging SRE on-call. Severity: P1.

sam: acked. I'm oncall, looking. Which clusters are affected?

maria: seeing errors from payment-service, auth-proxy, and service-discovery checks. SRV queries to consul return "SERVFAIL" intermittently.

isaac: Confirmed. CoreDNS pods in kube-system on us-west-3c nodes show repeated `read udp` timeouts in logs. Example: 
```
E0215 02:07:10.123456 core.go:123] plugin/errors: 2 0 "SERVFAIL"
201 02:07:10.123456 [INFO] query from 10.32.0.12:53214, name: _grpc._tcp.payment-service.svc.cluster.local., type: SRV
```

sam: any recent infra changes in that AZ? node upgrades, routing changes?

netops: we pushed a BGP flapping mitigation in us-west-3 yesterday night (control-plane only). No intentional changes to DNS forwarding. Checking forwarding IPs now.

deploy-bot: rolling deploy started: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/coredns -n kube-system` (canary) at 02:12 UTC.

elaine: before doing mass restart, can we add a static fallback for critical SRV entries so services don't fail while we investigate?

ops-sre: good call. I added a temporary ConfigMap with static SRV entries for `auth-proxy` and `payment-service` and updated their DNS configs to use it. Patch applied via `kubectl apply -f /tmp/srv-fallback.yaml`

maria: quick metrics — service discovery error rate peaked ~02:05 UTC at ~18% for internal SRV resolutions in that AZ. Latency for successful SRV lookups increased from 20ms to ~1.2s.

isaac: digging into CoreDNS upstream resolution: forwarding to node-local resolver sometimes returns RCODE=2. Also seeing `connection refused` to Consul agents on some nodes.

sam: can we isolate whether it's CoreDNS -> Consul or node-level networking? Please run `dig @127.0.0.1 -p 8600 _grpc._tcp.payment-service.service.consul SRV` on an affected node.

isaac: ran `dig` on node-azb-12: response intermittent, sometimes fine, often `SERVFAIL`. Node-level logs show repeated `iptables` conntrack drops: `nf_conntrack: table full`.

netops: ah — we saw spike in short-lived connections yesterday from a few pods. Conntrack table may be exhausted on some nodes. Increasing `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` on affected nodes now. Applying via cloud-init patch to the ASG to roll through nodes.

sam: can we reduce churn immediately? Any noisy pods causing many short connections?

elaine: payment-service consumer clients had a retry storm after initial failures, which amplified connections. We throttled retries with a temporary config change (reduced concurrency) for the main client pool.

deploy-bot: canary CoreDNS restart showed improvement on that node: error rate dropped to ~3% for a short window. Proceeding to controlled rollout to remaining nodes in AZ (staggered 30s).

maria: Customer impact: internal product metrics show 7% of external API requests in us-west-3c had delayed backend lookups leading to 504s for ~15 minutes. No external customer-facing outage reported, but degraded performance for a subset of tenants. Logging flagged 12 high-traffic customers with repeated retries.

ops-sre: mitigation summary so far: 1) applied static SRV fallback for critical services 2) canary + staggered CoreDNS restarts 3) increased conntrack limit on affected nodes 4) temporarily throttled client retries 5) opened ticket with network team for kernel-level drops.

netops: looking at upstream network path — we saw asymmetric routing to the stub resolver in region for a subset of nodes; hitting a NAT gateway CPU spike. Spinning up standby NAT nodes and rebalancing.

sam: ETA on rebalancing and full node rollout?

netops: NAT rebalancing started, should be done in ~10m. Conntrack bump applied to all nodes in the AZ; nodes will pick up values on next config refresh (rolling).

isaac: monitoring shows SRV error rate back down to ~1.5% after second wave of restarts + NAT rebalance. Still sporadic failures creeping up at 5-min intervals — likely leftover noisy clients.

sam: mark incident as mitigated once sustained <2% errors for 15m. Continue to monitor, and do on-call handoff in 30m.

deploy-bot: `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns -o wide` at 02:45 UTC: all replicas RUNNING across AZ nodes.

maria: creating internal incident page and will notify CS for the 12 customers that had repeated retries. Draft: "Intermittent internal service discovery failures due to conntrack exhaustion + NAT imbalance in us-west-3c; mitigations applied; postmortem forthcoming."

elaine: I'll take the next 2-hour window for monitoring and write the initial timeline + immediate action items. Sam will lead the postmortem.

sam: handing off to @elaine for monitoring. Thanks everyone. Please add any remaining notes to the incident doc.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. New on-call: elaine. Previous on-call: sam.

isaac: follow-ups (short): - add conntrack and NAT saturation checks to runbook - lower SRV TTLs for critical services during rollouts - add graceful retry backoff default to client library - automate static SRV fallback application for P1s

maria: assigning owners in the doc. Ops-SRE for conntrack/runbook, NetOps for NAT scaling, DevEx for client retry defaults.

sam: closing notes: root cause: conntrack table exhaustion on subset of nodes in us-west-3c combined with NAT gateway CPU hotspot causing intermittent upstream resolver failures -> CoreDNS and Consul agent queries intermittently returning SERVFAIL leading to SRV lookup errors.

elaine: will keep monitoring until 04:00 UTC then update incident doc with timeline.

ops-sre: adding postmortem template link: https://intranet.redwood/postmortems/drafts/1859999999. Please don't share externally yet.

maria: thanks all. :thumbsup:
